entries.desc: List all files (including dotfiles) with human-readable sizes.
Switch back to the previous working directory.
Print the absolute path of the current directory.
Find files matching a pattern modified in the last 7 days.
Recursively grep for a pattern, line-numbered, skipping binary files.
Set file permissions to rw-r--r-- (owner can write, group/others read).
Change file owner and group.
List every process and grep for one. Use 'pgrep -fa' on modern systems.
Live view of CPU/memory usage by process. Press P (CPU) or M (memory) to sort.
Friendlier top alternative with mouse support and tree view (F5).
Force-terminate a process. Try kill PID first — SIGTERM lets the process clean up.
Show disk usage per mount point in human-readable units.
Show the size of each item in the current directory (sum subdirectories).
List listening TCP/UDP ports with the process holding each one. Replaces netstat.
Show a systemd unit's state, recent logs, and process tree.
entries.example: systemctl restart nginx && systemctl status nginx

entries.desc: Tail the logs of a systemd unit in real time.
Create a gzip-compressed tarball of a directory.
Mirror a directory over SSH, preserving permissions, compressing in flight.
Print the first field of each line. Brilliant for column-shaped data.
In-place replace 'foo' with 'bar' across a file.
List objects in an S3 bucket. Add --recursive to descend.
Upload a local file to S3. Add --acl public-read for static-site assets.
Sync a local directory to a bucket, transferring only changed files.
List EC2 instances in the current region. Use --filters to narrow.
Power on one or more stopped instances.
Show the IAM identity (user, account, ARN) used by the current credentials.
List the managed IAM policies attached to a given user.
Tail a CloudWatch log group in real time, much like 'tail -f'.
Pin the default region for subsequent CLI calls (or use AWS_REGION env var).
List every pod across all namespaces. Add -o wide for node + IP.
Show a pod's events, conditions, container statuses — the first stop when something is wrong.
Follow logs from a pod. Add -c CONTAINER to pick a sidecar.
Open an interactive shell inside a running container.
Create or update resources declared in a YAML manifest.
Tunnel a local port to a service for ad-hoc access.
Watch a deployment roll out; exits when stable. Use 'undo' to revert.
Pin the current kubectl context to a namespace so you can stop typing -n.
Show per-pod CPU/memory usage (requires metrics-server).
List recent cluster events — invaluable for figuring out why a pod won't schedule.
List every container (running and stopped) with status and ports.
Run a container interactively and delete it on exit.
Build an image from the Dockerfile in the current directory.
Attach a shell inside a running container.
Tail a container's stdout/stderr.
Reclaim disk by removing stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images.
Show working-tree state: staged, unstaged, untracked.
Compact branch-aware history for the last 20 commits.
Show what's queued for the next commit.
Create and switch to a new branch (modern alternative to 'git checkout -b').
Save uncommitted changes and clean the working tree. Restore with 'git stash pop'.
Replay the current branch on top of main. Use after pulling to keep history linear.
Undo the last commit, keeping changes in the working tree (--hard discards them).
Show who last touched lines 30-60 of a file and in which commit.
Verbose HTTP request — surfaces redirects, headers, TLS handshake.
Resolve a DNS name; +short prints just the answer.
Query a specific DNS resolver (here Google's 8.8.8.8) instead of the system default.
Show every hop between you and the target. Use 'mtr' for a live view.
Service-version scan of low ports. -sS for stealth SYN scan (root).
Capture packets on any interface for one port. -w saves to a pcap file.
List firewall rules with packet/byte counters and numeric addresses.
Open a raw TLS session — surfaces the certificate chain and supported ciphers.
Stream new lines appended to a file in real time — the standard way to watch a live log.
Page through a file without loading it all into memory; +F follows like tail -f (press Ctrl-C to scroll back).
Copy files or directories recursively while preserving permissions, ownership, and timestamps.
Create a directory tree, making any missing parent directories without erroring if they already exist.
Create a symbolic link pointing to a target file or directory; common for atomic release switches.
Show detailed file metadata — size, permissions, inode, and access/modify/change timestamps.
Copy files securely between local and remote machines over SSH.
Open a secure remote shell; add -p for a custom port or -i to specify an identity key.
Edit the current user's cron jobs; use crontab -l to list and crontab -r to remove them.
List open files and the processes holding them — handy for finding what owns a network port.
Show total, used, free, and cached memory plus swap in human-readable units.
Display all network interfaces with their IP addresses and state; the modern replacement for ifconfig.
Build and run commands from items piped on stdin; use -0 with find -print0 for filenames with spaces.
Re-run a command at a fixed interval and refresh its output in place — useful for monitoring a changing value.
Power off one or more running instances. Add --hibernate on supported types.
Launch a new EC2 instance from an AMI. Pass --key-name and --security-group-ids to make it reachable.
entries.example: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0abcd1234 --instance-type t3.micro --key-name mykey --count 1

entries.desc: List security groups and their inbound/outbound rules. Use --group-ids to target one.
List VPCs in the current region, including CIDR blocks and the default-VPC flag.
Delete an object from S3. Add --recursive to remove a whole prefix.
Generate a time-limited signed URL for temporary download access to a private object.
Create a new programmatic access key pair for an IAM user (secret shown once).
Attach a managed policy to an IAM role to grant it permissions.
Assume a role and receive temporary credentials, typically for cross-account access.
Invoke a Lambda function and write the response payload to a file. Add --payload for input.
entries.example: aws lambda invoke --function-name myfn --payload '{"k":"v"}' --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out out.json

entries.desc: Read a single item from a DynamoDB table by its primary key.

entries.cmd: aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <acct>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
entries.desc: Authenticate the local Docker client against a private ECR registry.
entries.example: aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 111122223333.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

entries.desc: Add an EKS cluster to your local kubeconfig so kubectl can talk to it.
Open an interactive shell to an instance via Session Manager — no SSH key or open port needed.
Fetch a value from SSM Parameter Store, decrypting SecureString parameters.
Retrieve the current value of a secret stored in Secrets Manager.
entries.example: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/api-key --query SecretString --output text

entries.desc: List pods, services, deployments, replicasets and statefulsets in a namespace in one shot.
List cluster nodes with their internal/external IPs, OS image, kernel and container runtime.
Delete the resources defined in a manifest, or delete by type and name.
Manually set the number of replicas for a deployment, replicaset or statefulset.
Update a container image on a deployment to trigger a rolling update.
Imperatively create a deployment from a container image.
Create a service to expose a deployment, pod or replicaset on a port.
Start a single pod from an image — handy for one-off debugging containers.
Add or update a label on a resource; append - to a key to remove it.
Dump the full live spec of a resource as YAML for inspection or export.
entries.example: kubectl get deployment api -o yaml > api.yaml

entries.desc: Show the API schema and field documentation for a resource — great for writing manifests.
Cordon a node and evict its pods before maintenance; use uncordon to bring it back.
Add a taint so only pods with a matching toleration schedule onto the node.
Apply a partial update to a live resource without editing the whole manifest.
Check whether the current user (or another via --as) is allowed to perform an action.
Create a generic secret from literal values or files for use as env vars or volumes.
List locally stored images with their tags, sizes, and IDs.
Download an image (or a specific tag) from a registry.
Upload a tagged image to a remote registry.
Gracefully stop a running container by sending SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after a timeout).
Remove one or more stopped containers.
Delete an image from local storage by name or ID.
Create a new tag (alias) that points at an existing image.
Print low-level JSON metadata about a container, image, network, or volume.
Live-stream CPU, memory, and network usage for running containers.
Copy files or folders between a container and the host.
List all Docker networks and their drivers.
List all Docker-managed volumes.
Build, create, and start all services defined in compose.yaml in the background.
Stop and remove the containers, networks, and default services created by 'up'.
Copy a remote repository, including its full history, to a new local directory.
Stage changed files so they are included in the next commit.
Record the staged snapshot to history with a message.
Upload local commits on a branch to its remote counterpart.
Fetch from the remote and merge the changes into the current branch.
Download remote refs and objects without merging, pruning deleted remote branches.
Join the history of another branch into the current one.
Discard working-tree changes or unstage files (modern split from checkout).
Apply the changes from a specific commit onto the current branch.
Create an annotated tag marking a specific commit, typically a release.
List configured remote repositories and their fetch/push URLs.
Create a new commit that undoes a previous commit without rewriting history.
Delete untracked files and directories from the working tree.
Show the history of where HEAD and branch refs have pointed, useful for recovering lost commits.
Lists every network interface with its assigned IPv4/IPv6 addresses, MAC, and link state (modern replacement for ifconfig).
Prints the kernel routing table, including the default gateway used to reach external networks.
entries.example: ip route add 10.0.0.0/24 via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0

entries.cmd: ip link set dev eth0 up
entries.desc: Brings a network interface administratively up or down at the link layer.
entries.example: ip link set dev eth0 down

entries.desc: Sends a fixed count of ICMP echo requests to test reachability and round-trip latency to a host.
Combines ping and traceroute into a live, continuously updated per-hop report of latency and packet loss along a path.
Shows all listening TCP and UDP sockets with their ports and owning process (modern replacement for netstat).
Displays the ARP/neighbor table mapping IP addresses to MAC addresses on the local link.
Queries or changes physical NIC settings such as link speed, duplex, and auto-negotiation status.
entries.example: ethtool -s eth0 speed 1000 duplex full autoneg on

entries.desc: Performs a simple DNS lookup, resolving a hostname to its IP addresses or an IP back to a name.
Opens a raw TCP listener with netcat to test connectivity, transfer data, or debug a port.
Uses netcat in zero-I/O mode to check whether a specific TCP port on a host is open.
Creates an SSH local port-forward so a port on your machine tunnels through a gateway to a remote service.
Traces the route to a host and discovers the path MTU without requiring root privileges.
